summary: Cache hit-rate dropped after model update on Dedicated route; sudden cost increase traced to version_mismatch misses during rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Aurora Support (Dedicated) reported a sudden increase in inference cost and a noticeable latency shift immediately following a model update on their primary chat route. Initial hypothesis was a cache regression or telemetry issue; investigation showed a real cache efficiency drop driven by version_mismatch misses during a staged rollout that temporarily mixed model versions within the same dedicated pool.

Impact:
- Customer-reported cost increase: ~18–25% higher token charges per request (driven by higher prefill compute due to low reuse)
- Elevated p95 latency on prompts with repeated system + policy prefixes (customer expects high prefix reuse)
- Duration: ~6–10 hours (from rollout start until rollback / rollout policy adjusted)

Customer context:
- Deployment: Dedicated (single region)
- Workload: support-agent chat with long, stable system prompt and repeated policy prefix; high expected prefix/KV reuse across turns.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: us-east
- Route: aurora-prod-chat (gateway route id: rt_8f2c…)
- Model: rw-llama3.1-70b-instruct
- Rollout: model version update initiated by customer using “latest” (un-pinned) channel.

What we observed (internal):
- Cache hit-rate dashboard: sharp drop in kv_cache_hit_rate and prefix_cache_reuse_effectiveness starting ~2025-03-03 16:10 UTC.
- Miss reason breakdown: spike dominated by miss_reason=version_mismatch; secondary increase in miss_reason=capacity (likely a downstream effect of lower reuse increasing KV footprint / churn).
- No evidence of telemetry ingestion drop (counters present, tags intact; no sudden flatlines).
- Correlated to control-plane rollout event: two model versions served concurrently in the dedicated pool for several hours.

Root cause:
During the staged rollout, requests for the same route were served by a mixed fleet (old model version and new model version). Cache keys include model_version_id to prevent unsafe reuse across model variants. As a result:
- Prefix cache entries created under vA could not be reused when the request landed on vB (and vice versa).
- For multi-turn chat, subsequent turns were not consistently routed to the same model version, producing frequent version_mismatch misses and re-prefill.

Resolution:
- Immediate mitigation: set rollout to 0% (effectively revert to the prior version) to restore consistent model_version_id across the pool; hit-rate recovered within ~30–60 minutes as cache warmed.
- Follow-up change (customer configuration guidance): pin the route to a specific model version during rollouts, or enable “sticky version routing” for the rollout window (avoid mixing versions within a single route unless explicitly testing cache impact).
- Customer confirmed cost/latency returned to baseline after mitigation.

Notes:
This is expected behavior given cache safety rules, but the customer experience was surprising because they assumed a staged rollout would be transparent to cache behavior. We should update Dedicated rollout guidance: mixing versions will reduce cache reuse and can increase cost, especially for workloads with stable prefixes.

Customer-facing message (approved by CS):
We explained that cache reuse is intentionally version-scoped for correctness; during the window where two versions were live, reuse dropped. Recommended pinning during rollouts or scheduling rollouts during low-traffic windows, and (if they want canary) routing canary traffic to a separate route to isolate cache impact.
comments: 2025-03-03 17:02 UTC (Owen Phillips, Support): Customer reports ‘cost jumped ~20% after yesterday’s model update’ and ‘responses feel slower’ on Dedicated. Asked for timeframe, route name, and whether they pinned model version or used latest.

2025-03-03 17:18 UTC (Customer - Aurora): Change was applied around 16:00 UTC. They use the ‘latest’ channel for rw-llama3.1-70b-instruct. Noted stable system prompt and expected caching to keep costs low.

2025-03-03 17:35 UTC (Allison Grant, Observability): Checked cache hit-rate dashboards for rt_8f2c…: hit-rate down sharply; miss reasons show large version_mismatch starting ~16:10 UTC. No sign of metrics pipeline drop. Shared screenshot + query in #eng-sre.

2025-03-03 17:52 UTC (Ethan Park, Platform Tagging): Confirmed model_version_id tag is present and consistent; join between gateway route id and runtime metrics looks correct. Likely real mixed-version rollout behavior.

2025-03-03 18:10 UTC (Omar El-Sayed, Runtime): Sanity check: version_mismatch misses are expected if requests bounce across versions; cache keys include model_version_id. Suggested mitigation: avoid mixing versions for a single high-reuse route, or use sticky routing during rollout.

2025-03-03 18:22 UTC (Connor O'Brien, Releases): Reviewed dedicated rollout settings: rollout set to 50/50 for several hours (customer-initiated). Proposed: revert to 0% / old version immediately, then re-run rollout with pinning or separate canary route.

2025-03-03 18:40 UTC (Owen Phillips, Support -> Customer): Explained findings: cache reuse is version-scoped; during rollout with mixed versions, hit-rate dropped leading to higher prefill and cost. Proposed immediate rollback to restore baseline and then plan a safer rollout strategy.
2025-03-03 19:05 UTC (Customer - Aurora): Approved rollback / revert. They want guidance on how to canary without impacting overall cost.
2025-03-03 19:20 UTC (Connor O'Brien, Releases): Rollout set to 0% (old version only). Monitoring hit-rate recovery.

2025-03-03 20:05 UTC (Allison Grant, Observability): Hit-rate trending back up; version_mismatch miss reason returned to near-zero. p95 latency improving. Marked incident mitigated; continue monitoring for 2 hours.
2025-03-04 10:12 UTC (Miguel Santos, CS): Customer confirms cost/latency back to baseline overnight. Requested a written best-practices note for future rollouts (pinning vs canary route split).

2025-03-06 16:30 UTC (Owen Phillips, Support): Added guidance to customer: (1) pin model version for primary prod route; (2) create a separate canary route with new version; (3) optionally enable sticky routing to version during rollout if they must canary on same route; (4) schedule rollouts during low traffic to reduce cache warmup cost.

2025-03-07 09:15 UTC (Allison Grant, Observability): Closed loop: no additional anomalies. Recommendation: add a lightweight console note / doc callout that mixed-version rollouts reduce cache reuse and can increase cost for prefix-heavy workloads.
resolution: Rollback to a single model version in the dedicated pool eliminated version_mismatch cache misses. Provided rollout best practices to prevent mixed-version routing for high-reuse routes (pin model versions or isolate canary to separate route / enable sticky version routing).
next_steps: Support: send customer a short ‘Dedicated rollout + caching’ FAQ (owner: Owen Phillips).
Product/Platform: add a warning in rollout UI/docs when serving multiple model versions for a single route can degrade cache efficiency (owner: Paula Mendes to triage).
SRE/Obs: consider an internal guardrail alert on sustained spikes in miss_reason=version_mismatch for Dedicated routes to catch similar cases earlier (owner: Aisha Bello to propose thresholds).
